fields.title: Software Developer
fields.description: Software developers design, build, and maintain the applications and systems that power our digital world — from mobile banking apps to hospital management systems.
fields.duties:
• Write, test, and debug code in languages such as Python, JavaScript, Java, or Kotlin
• Design software architecture and database schemas
• Collaborate with product managers and designers
• Review code written by peers and mentor junior developers
• Deploy and monitor applications in cloud environments (AWS, GCP, Azure)
• Maintain and improve existing systems to ensure reliability and performance
fields.skills_required:
• Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, JavaScript, Java)
• Problem-solving and logical thinking
• Version control with Git
• Knowledge of databases (SQL/NoSQL)
• Communication and teamwork skills
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Aim for B+ or above, especially in Mathematics and Sciences
2. Bachelor of Science in Computer Science / Software Engineering (4 years)
   — Available at UoN, KU, JKUAT, Strathmore, Maseno
3. Industry certifications: AWS, Google Cloud, Meta Developer
4. Build a portfolio of 3–5 real projects on GitHub
5. Internship or attachment during 3rd year
6. Entry-level roles: Junior Developer → Mid-level → Senior → Tech Lead
fields.job_opportunities:
• Fintech companies (M-Pesa, Equity Bank, KCB, Safaricom)
• Tech startups in Silicon Savannah (Nairobi)
• Global companies via remote work (Google, Microsoft, Amazon)
• Government agencies (eCitizen, NTSA, IEBC)
• NGOs and development organisations (USAID, UNICEF)
• Freelance & consultancy work
fields.future_outlook: Kenya's tech sector is booming. Nairobi's Silicon Savannah is Africa's leading startup hub, and demand for software developers is growing 30% annually. Remote work has opened global opportunities with USD-denominated salaries. AI and cloud skills will be critical by 2030.

fields.title: Data Scientist
fields.description: Data scientists extract insights from large datasets to drive business decisions, using statistics, machine learning, and programming to turn raw data into actionable intelligence.
fields.duties:
• Collect, clean, and process large datasets from multiple sources
• Build machine learning and AI models for prediction and classification
• Create data visualisations and dashboards for stakeholders
• Collaborate with engineering teams to deploy ML models
• Write reports and present findings to non-technical executives
• Stay current with AI/ML research and best practices
fields.skills_required:
• Python or R programming
• Statistics and probability
• Machine learning frameworks (TensorFlow, scikit-learn, PyTorch)
• SQL and big data tools (Spark, BigQuery)
• Data visualisation (Tableau, Power BI, Matplotlib)
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Sciences are essential
2. BSc Statistics / Mathematics / Computer Science / Data Science (4 years)
   — JKUAT, UoN, Strathmore offer relevant programmes
3. MSc Data Science (optional but competitive advantage)
4. Online certifications: Google Data Analytics, Coursera ML Specialisation
5. Kaggle competitions to build public portfolio
6. Internship at a bank, telco, or research org
fields.job_opportunities:
• Commercial banks (Equity, KCB, Cooperative Bank)
• Telecommunications (Safaricom, Airtel)
• Government statistical agencies (KNBS, KRA)
• International NGOs and research institutions
• E-commerce platforms (Jumia, Glovo)
• Global remote roles with USD salaries
fields.future_outlook: AI and data science are the fastest-growing fields globally. In Kenya, banks, telcos, and government agencies are investing heavily in data infrastructure. Professionals with Python + ML skills command the highest salaries in the tech sector.

fields.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
fields.description: Cybersecurity analysts protect organisations' digital assets from hackers, data breaches, and cyber threats — a critical role as Kenya's digital economy grows rapidly.
fields.duties:
• Monitor networks and systems for security breaches and intrusions
• Conduct vulnerability assessments and penetration tests
• Respond to security incidents and coordinate recovery
• Develop and enforce security policies
• Train staff on cybersecurity awareness
• Research emerging threats and recommend countermeasures
fields.skills_required:
• Network fundamentals (TCP/IP, firewalls, VPNs)
• Security tools: Wireshark, Metasploit, Nmap, SIEM
• Programming knowledge (Python, Bash scripting)
• Risk assessment and threat modelling
• Incident response and digital forensics
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Physics are important
2. BSc Information Technology / Computer Science / Cybersecurity (4 years)
3. Professional certifications: CEH, CompTIA Security+, CISSP, OSCP
4. Practice on platforms: TryHackMe, HackTheBox, PicoCTF
5. Entry roles: Security Analyst → Senior Analyst → CISO
fields.job_opportunities:
• Banks and financial institutions
• Government agencies (KRA, NTSA, Communications Authority)
• Telecommunications companies
• Cybersecurity firms and consulting companies
• International organisations and embassies
• Remote security roles for global firms
fields.future_outlook: Cybercrime is growing globally and Kenya is no exception. The Communications Authority has mandated cybersecurity standards for all critical infrastructure. Demand for qualified security professionals far exceeds supply — making this one of the most lucrative and future-proof career paths in Kenya's tech sector.

fields.title: Network Engineer
fields.description: Network engineers design, implement, and maintain the communication networks that connect people and organisations — from enterprise LAN networks to national fibre infrastructure.
fields.duties:
• Design and implement LAN, WAN, and wireless network infrastructure
• Configure routers, switches, firewalls, and access points
• Monitor network performance and troubleshoot connectivity issues
• Plan network capacity and upgrades
• Maintain documentation of network topology
• Support voice over IP (VoIP) and video conferencing systems
fields.skills_required:
• Networking protocols (TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, VLANs)
• Cisco, Juniper, or Huawei hardware configuration
• Network security fundamentals
• Linux and Windows Server administration
• Problem-solving under pressure
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Physics essential
2. BSc Telecommunications / Computer Science / IT (4 years)
3. Certifications: CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Network+
4. Entry roles: Network Support Technician → Network Administrator → Network Engineer
fields.job_opportunities:
• Internet Service Providers (Safaricom, Telkom, Airtel, Faiba)
• Banks and financial institutions
• Government ICT departments
• Large corporations with multi-site networks
• ISPs and data centres
• Telecommunications consulting firms
fields.future_outlook: Kenya's broadband expansion and the roll-out of 5G networks will require thousands of network engineers over the next decade. Cloud networking and SD-WAN skills are becoming increasingly critical as organisations move to hybrid cloud infrastructure.

fields.title: Medical Doctor (Physician)
fields.description: Medical doctors diagnose and treat illnesses, prescribe medication, and guide patients through preventive care — one of the most respected and impactful careers in Kenya.
fields.duties:
• Examine patients and take detailed medical histories
• Diagnose diseases and order diagnostic tests
• Prescribe and administer treatments and medications
• Perform minor surgical procedures
• Refer complex cases to specialists
• Document patient records and maintain confidentiality
• Educate patients and communities on disease prevention
fields.skills_required:
• Deep knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology
• Clinical examination and diagnostic skills
• Empathy and excellent communication
• Decision-making under pressure
• Attention to detail and analytical thinking
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum B+ (mean grade); Biology, Chemistry essential
2. MBChB (Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery) — 6 years
   — University of Nairobi, Moi University, Egerton, KU, Mt Kenya University
3. 1-year internship (mandatory, government hospitals)
4. 2-year community service (mandatory)
5. Optional: Postgraduate specialisation (3–5 years) — Surgery, Paediatrics, etc.
6. Registration with Kenya Medical Practitioners Board (KMPDB)
fields.job_opportunities:
• Government hospitals (KNH, Moi Teaching, county hospitals)
• Private hospitals (Aga Khan, Nairobi Hospital, MP Shah, Avenue)
• NGO health programmes (MSF, AMREF, Red Cross)
• International organisations (WHO, UNICEF)
• Private clinical practice
• Medical research institutions
fields.future_outlook: Kenya faces a severe doctor shortage — 1 doctor per 10,000 people versus the WHO recommended 1 per 1,000. Universal Health Coverage (UHC) implementation is creating unprecedented demand. Specialist doctors in surgery, oncology, and cardiology are especially needed.

fields.title: Clinical Officer
fields.description: Clinical officers provide primary healthcare services, diagnose common illnesses, and manage outpatient care — they are the backbone of Kenya's healthcare system.
fields.duties:
• Conduct patient consultations and physical examinations
• Diagnose and treat common diseases (malaria, TB, diabetes, hypertension)
• Prescribe medications and manage treatment plans
• Conduct minor surgical procedures
• Refer complex cases to doctors or specialists
• Provide maternal and child health services
• Maintain accurate patient records
fields.skills_required:
• Clinical examination and diagnostic skills
• Knowledge of pharmacology and treatment protocols
• Emergency response and patient management
• Communication and patient counselling
• Teamwork in clinical settings
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade); Biology and Chemistry essential
2. Diploma in Clinical Medicine & Surgery (3 years) at KMTC
3. Or Upgrade to Bachelor of Science in Clinical Medicine (2 more years)
4. Registration with Clinical Officers Council of Kenya (COC-K)
5. Specialisation options: Anaesthesia, Orthopaedics, Ophthalmology
fields.job_opportunities:
• Ministry of Health hospitals and dispensaries
• County health facilities across Kenya
• KMTC campuses as clinical instructors
• NGO health programmes in underserved areas
• Private clinics and health centres
• Military and National Police health services
fields.future_outlook: Clinical officers fill a critical gap in Kenya's healthcare system. With over 88 KMTC campuses producing graduates, there is growing demand especially in rural and underserved areas under UHC. Specialised COs in anaesthesia command significantly higher pay.

fields.title: Registered Nurse
fields.description: Nurses provide compassionate direct patient care, administer treatments, monitor health, and are the largest professional group in Kenya's health workforce.
fields.duties:
• Administer medications and monitor vital signs
• Provide wound care, IV therapy, and bedside care
• Collaborate with doctors on treatment plans
• Educate patients and families on health management
• Maintain accurate nursing records
• Support patients during surgeries and procedures
• Respond to medical emergencies on the ward
fields.skills_required:
• Clinical nursing skills and patient assessment
• Compassion and emotional resilience
• Communication with patients and multidisciplinary teams
• Critical thinking in emergencies
• Infection control and patient safety protocols
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade); Biology and Chemistry are key
2. Option A: Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN) — 3 years at KMTC
3. Option B: BSc Nursing — 4 years (Moi, UoN, JKUAT, KU)
4. Option C: Kenya Enrolled Nurse (KEN) — 2 years at KMTC (entry with C-)
5. Registration with Nursing Council of Kenya (NCK)
6. Specialisation: ICU, Midwifery, Paediatric Nursing, Oncology
fields.job_opportunities:
• Government and county hospitals
• Private hospitals and nursing homes
• Community health programmes
• International health missions (MSF, Red Cross)
• Diaspora nursing in UK, USA, UAE, Canada (highly sought after)
• School and corporate occupational health
fields.future_outlook: Kenya has a critical nursing shortage, and international demand is equally high. Thousands of Kenyan nurses work abroad (UK NHS, US hospitals) earning significantly higher salaries. Specialised nurses in ICU, theatre, and midwifery earn the most.

fields.title: Pharmacist
fields.description: Pharmacists ensure safe medication use by dispensing prescriptions, counselling patients, and advising healthcare teams on drug therapy — a science-heavy, patient-facing role.
fields.duties:
• Dispense prescription medications accurately
• Counsel patients on correct dosage, side effects, and interactions
• Review prescriptions for errors or contraindications
• Manage pharmaceutical inventory and cold chain
• Collaborate with doctors on complex medication regimens
• Compound specialised medications as needed
• Ensure compliance with pharmaceutical regulations
fields.skills_required:
• Deep knowledge of pharmacology and therapeutics
• Attention to detail (medication errors can be fatal)
• Patient communication and counselling
• Chemistry knowledge
• Inventory management and business skills (for pharmacy owners)
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum B (mean grade); Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics essential
2. Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) — 5 years (UoN, MTRH, Strathmore SMPC)
3. 1-year internship in a registered pharmacy or hospital
4. Registration with Pharmacy and Poisons Board Kenya
5. Optional: Masters in Clinical Pharmacy or Pharmaceutical Sciences
fields.job_opportunities:
• Hospital pharmacies (KNH, Aga Khan, private hospitals)
• Community pharmacies (Chain pharmacies: Goodlife, Haltons, Medivet)
• Pharmaceutical manufacturing companies
• KEMSA and drug regulatory authorities
• NGO health supply chain programmes
• Academic and research institutions
fields.future_outlook: The pharmaceutical sector in Kenya is growing with local manufacturing expanding and UHC driving increased medicine access. Community pharmacy ownership is highly lucrative for entrepreneurial pharmacists. Global demand, especially in the Gulf states, also offers excellent opportunities.

fields.title: Civil Engineer
fields.description: Civil engineers plan, design, and supervise the construction of Kenya's infrastructure — roads, bridges, dams, buildings, and water systems that drive national development.
fields.duties:
• Design and draft engineering plans for structures and infrastructure
• Conduct site surveys and soil/material testing
• Supervise construction projects and manage contractors
• Ensure structures meet safety and environmental standards
• Prepare cost estimates and project schedules
• Conduct structural inspections and quality control
• Liaise with government, clients, and project stakeholders
fields.skills_required:
• Mathematics, physics, and structural analysis
• AutoCAD and civil engineering design software
• Project management and leadership
• Knowledge of building codes and regulations
• Problem-solving and decision-making
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum B+ (mean grade); Mathematics and Physics are critical
2. BSc Civil Engineering — 5 years (UoN, JKUAT, TU-K, Dedan Kimathi)
3. Graduate Engineer attachment/internship
4. Graduate membership: Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK)
5. Professional Engineer (PE) registration after 3 years experience
6. Optional: MSc Structural / Geotechnical / Water Resources Engineering
fields.job_opportunities:
• Ministry of Public Works and Housing
• Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA)
• Construction companies and real estate developers
• Consulting engineering firms (Arup, Knight Frank, Mott MacDonald Kenya)
• County governments for infrastructure projects
• NGOs and development banks (World Bank, AfDB projects)
fields.future_outlook: Kenya's infrastructure boom — Vision 2030 projects, affordable housing programme, and SGR expansion — means sustained high demand for civil engineers. Specialising in structural or transport engineering and getting registered PE status significantly boosts earning potential.

fields.title: Electrical Engineer
fields.description: Electrical engineers design and maintain electrical systems — from power generation and distribution networks to electronic control systems and renewable energy installations.
fields.duties:
• Design electrical systems for buildings, factories, and power plants
• Install and maintain transformers, switchgear, and distribution panels
• Work on solar PV, wind, and hydro renewable energy projects
• Troubleshoot electrical faults and power quality issues
• Ensure compliance with electrical safety regulations
• Supervise electrical contractors and technicians
fields.skills_required:
• Circuit design and power systems analysis
• AutoCAD Electrical and ETAP software
• Knowledge of Kenya Power grid standards
• Renewable energy systems (solar, wind)
• Safety standards and electrical codes
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Physics are essential
2. BSc Electrical Engineering / Electrical & Electronics Engineering — 5 years
   (JKUAT, UoN, TU-K, Dedan Kimathi University)
3. Graduate engineer registration with Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK)
4. Renewable energy certifications: SEAI, IRENA training
5. Professional Engineer registration after 3 years
fields.job_opportunities:
• Kenya Power & Lighting Company (KPLC)
• Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen)
• Rural Electrification Authority
• Solar energy companies (Solar Africa, Azuri Technologies)
• Construction and real estate firms
• Manufacturing plants and industrial facilities
fields.future_outlook: Kenya's renewable energy target (100% clean energy by 2030) and the Last Mile Connectivity project are creating massive demand for electrical engineers. Solar energy is booming with off-grid electrification projects expanding across rural Kenya.

fields.title: Accountant (CPA)
fields.description: Accountants manage financial records, prepare reports, ensure tax compliance, and help organisations make sound financial decisions — a core role in every business.
fields.duties:
• Prepare financial statements (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow)
• Manage accounts payable and receivable
• Conduct internal and external audits
• Prepare and file tax returns (PAYE, VAT, Corporate Tax)
• Advise management on cost control and financial planning
• Maintain compliance with IFRS and Kenya Revenue Authority rules
• Prepare payroll and benefits administration
fields.skills_required:
• Financial reporting and analysis
• Accounting software (QuickBooks, Sage, SAP, Xero)
• Tax legislation knowledge (Kenya Revenue Authority)
• Attention to detail and integrity
• Communication and presentation skills
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics B+ recommended; Commerce subjects helpful
2. Option A: BCom / BSc Accounting (4 years) — KU, USIU, Strathmore, UoN
3. Option B: CPA Kenya (Certified Public Accountant) — KASNEB exams (3 levels)
4. ICPAK membership after completing CPA-K
5. Optional: ACCA, CIMA for international credibility
6. MBA for senior management roles
fields.job_opportunities:
• Audit firms (Deloitte, KPMG, PWC, EY — 'Big Four' in Nairobi)
• Banks and financial institutions
• Manufacturing and retail companies
• Government ministries and parastatals
• NGOs and development organisations
• Entrepreneurial: Start your own CPA practice
fields.future_outlook: Every organisation needs accountants. ICPAK membership significantly raises earning potential. Big Four audit firms are the gateway to top careers. Kenya's growing SME sector creates huge demand for affordable accounting services — entrepreneurial CPAs can build thriving practices.

fields.title: Advocate / Lawyer
fields.description: Advocates advise clients on legal matters, draft contracts and legal documents, and represent clients in courts — a prestigious career at the heart of justice.
fields.duties:
• Advise clients on their legal rights and obligations
• Draft contracts, wills, and legal agreements
• Represent clients in civil and criminal court proceedings
• Conduct legal research and build case arguments
• Negotiate settlements and mediate disputes
• Ensure compliance with Kenyan statutes and regulations
• Protect client confidentiality at all times
fields.skills_required:
• Deep knowledge of Kenyan law (Constitutional, Commercial, Criminal, Family)
• Analytical reasoning and research skills
• Oral and written advocacy
• Negotiation and persuasion
• Time management across multiple cases
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum B+ (mean grade); Languages and Arts subjects beneficial
2. LLB (Bachelor of Laws) — 4 years (UoN, KU, Strathmore, USIU, Kabarak)
3. Kenya School of Law (KSL) — 1-year Advocates Training Programme (ATP)
4. Bar Examination and admission to the Roll of Advocates
5. Pupillage at a law firm (6 months)
6. Optional: LLM for specialisation (Commercial Law, International Law, IP)
fields.job_opportunities:
• Private law firms (Oraro, Anjarwalla, Kaplan & Stratton)
• Corporate legal departments (banks, multinationals)
• State Law Office (Attorney General's office)
• DPP and prosecution services
• NGOs and human rights organisations
• Judiciary (Magistrate → Judge pathway)
fields.future_outlook: Kenya's growing economy and complex regulatory environment create strong demand for commercial lawyers. Specialisation in fintech, land law, or environmental law is highly lucrative. Senior partners at top firms earn millions monthly.

fields.title: Secondary School Teacher
fields.description: Secondary school teachers shape the next generation by teaching KCSE subjects, mentoring students, and preparing them for higher education and life.
fields.duties:
• Prepare and deliver lessons aligned to the Kenya Curriculum (KICD)
• Evaluate student progress through assignments, tests, and exams
• Provide individualised support to struggling learners
• Prepare students for KCSE national examinations
• Maintain student records and communicate with parents
• Participate in school co-curricular activities and administration
• Continuously update subject knowledge and teaching methodology
fields.skills_required:
• Deep subject knowledge in teaching specialisation
• Lesson planning and curriculum delivery
• Classroom management and student motivation
• Assessment and feedback skills
• Patience, empathy, and communication
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Minimum C+ (mean grade); Strong grades in chosen subjects
2. Bachelor of Education (BEd) — 4 years, choose 2 teaching subjects
   — KU, Moi, Egerton, UoN, TU-K, Maseno, many private universities
3. Teacher Service Commission (TSC) registration and certification
4. Optional: MEd for HOD, Deputy Principal, or Principal roles
5. International teaching options: UK, Middle East with international schools
fields.job_opportunities:
• TSC-employed public secondary schools (47 counties)
• Private secondary schools and international schools
• National schools (Starehe, Alliance, Mang'u, Limuru)
• International schools in Nairobi (IB, IGCSE curriculum)
• Online tutoring platforms
• Teacher training colleges
fields.future_outlook: CBC implementation is creating demand for retrained and newly-qualified teachers. International schools in Kenya pay significantly more than TSC scales. Diaspora teaching in the UK, Middle East, and East Asia is a growing trend for Kenyan teachers seeking higher income.

fields.title: Economist
fields.description: Economists analyse economic data, model policy impacts, forecast trends, and advise governments, corporations, and international organisations on financial and social policy.
fields.duties:
• Analyse economic indicators: inflation, GDP, employment, trade balance
• Build econometric models to forecast economic trends
• Assess the impact of government policies
• Prepare economic research reports and policy briefs
• Advise on pricing, investment, and resource allocation decisions
• Monitor global economic developments and their local impact
fields.skills_required:
• Statistical analysis and econometrics (STATA, R, Python)
• Economic theory (micro and macro)
• Research and report writing
• Data visualisation and presentation
• Critical thinking and policy analysis
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Strong Mathematics is essential
2. BSc Economics or BA Economics — 4 years (UoN, KU, Strathmore, USIU, Moi)
3. MSc Economics or MBA for senior roles
4. Professional certifications: CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst)
5. PhD for research or university positions
fields.job_opportunities:
• Central Bank of Kenya (CBK)
• Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA)
• World Bank, IMF, UN Economic Commission for Africa
• Commercial banks and investment firms
• Research institutions (KIPPRA, IPAR)
• Consulting firms (McKinsey, Deloitte, KPMG)
fields.future_outlook: Kenya's integration into regional and global markets, combined with complex policy challenges (debt management, inflation, poverty reduction), creates strong demand for well-trained economists. International organisations pay extremely competitive salaries.

fields.title: Agronomist
fields.description: Agronomists apply science to improve crop production — advising farmers on seeds, soil, fertilisers, and pest management to boost yields and food security in Kenya.
fields.duties:
• Conduct soil testing and analysis
• Advise farmers on crop selection and rotation for their land
• Recommend fertiliser and irrigation programmes
• Diagnose and treat crop pests and diseases
• Conduct field trials on new seed varieties
• Train smallholder farmers on modern farming methods
• Work with agri-input companies to introduce new products
fields.skills_required:
• Soil science and plant biology
• Crop protection (IPM, pesticide management)
• GIS and precision agriculture tools
• Communication and farmer training skills
• Business acumen for agribusiness roles
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Biology, Chemistry, Agriculture subjects are important
2. BSc Agronomy / Agriculture / Crop Science — 4 years (Egerton, UoN, JKUAT)
3. Higher Diploma in Agriculture (for extension officer roles)
4. Optional: MSc Agronomy or Plant Pathology
5. Membership: Agrochemicals Association of Kenya
fields.job_opportunities:
• Ministry of Agriculture extension services
• County agriculture departments
• Agri-input companies (Yara, Syngenta, MEA Fertilizers)
• Large-scale farms (flower farms, tea estates, horticulture)
• NGOs and international development organisations
• Agribusiness startups and cooperatives
fields.future_outlook: Climate change is making agronomy knowledge more critical for Kenya's farming sector. Precision agriculture and digital farming are the future. With 70% of Kenyans depending on agriculture, the sector needs urgently modernised expertise.

fields.title: Environmental Scientist
fields.description: Environmental scientists study ecosystems, assess pollution, and advise on sustainability to protect Kenya's natural resources while enabling responsible economic development.
fields.duties:
• Conduct Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) for development projects
• Monitor water, soil, and air quality
• Advise on waste management and pollution control
• Support climate change adaptation and mitigation plans
• Work with NEMA on environmental compliance
• Research biodiversity and ecosystem health
fields.skills_required:
• Environmental chemistry and ecology
• GIS and remote sensing tools
• Environmental law and NEMA regulations
• Research and scientific writing
• Stakeholder engagement
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Biology, Chemistry, Geography helpful
2. BSc Environmental Science / Natural Resources / Ecology — 4 years
   (Moi, UoN, JKUAT, Kenyatta, Egerton)
3. Lead Expert registration with NEMA for EIA practice
4. MSc Environmental Management or Climate Change
5. Professional membership: Environmental Institute of Kenya (EIK)
fields.job_opportunities:
• National Environment Management Authority (NEMA)
• Kenya Forest Service and Kenya Wildlife Service
• Environmental consultancy firms
• Mining and oil companies (environmental compliance)
• NGOs (WWF Kenya, Nature Kenya, GreenBelt Movement)
• International organisations (UNEP headquarters in Nairobi)
fields.future_outlook: Nairobi hosts UNEP headquarters — giving Kenya a unique position in global environmental governance. EIA requirements for all major projects drive strong demand for environmental consultants. Climate change careers will explode globally in the next decade.

fields.title: Journalist & Media Personality
fields.description: Journalists investigate and report stories that inform and hold power to account — from TV anchors to investigative reporters, digital content creators, and podcast hosts.
fields.duties:
• Research, investigate, and verify news stories
• Conduct interviews and gather information from sources
• Write, edit, and present news articles or broadcasts
• Create multimedia content (video, podcast, social media)
• Build and maintain a network of contacts and sources
• Adhere to journalistic ethics and editorial standards
fields.skills_required:
• Strong writing and storytelling skills
• Research and investigative ability
• Broadcast presentation (for TV/radio)
• Video production and editing
• Social media and digital journalism skills
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Languages (English, Kiswahili) are key; minimum C+
2. BA Mass Communication / Journalism — 4 years (UoN, USIU, Daystar, Moi)
3. Or Diploma in Journalism (2–3 years at KIB, KIMC)
4. Internship at a media house (Nation, Standard, KBC, NTV, Citizen)
5. Build portfolio: articles, videos, podcast episodes
fields.job_opportunities:
• Nation Media Group, Standard Group, Royal Media Services
• KBC and county radio stations
• Digital media startups
• International media (BBC Africa, CNN, Al Jazeera Kenya)
• Corporate communications and PR departments
• Freelance digital content creation (YouTube, podcast, blogs)
fields.future_outlook: Digital journalism and content creation are transforming media. YouTubers, podcasters, and digital journalists can earn far more than traditional media salaries. Investigative journalism and data journalism are growing fields. Media personalities with strong social media presence are highly valued.

fields.title: Graphic Designer & Creative Director
fields.description: Graphic designers create visual communications — logos, branding, UI designs, marketing materials, and digital content — that shape how businesses look and feel.
fields.duties:
• Design logos, brand identities, and visual guidelines
• Create marketing materials: brochures, banners, social media graphics
• Design user interfaces for apps and websites (UI/UX)
• Collaborate with marketing teams on campaigns
• Prepare files for print and digital production
• Pitch creative concepts to clients
fields.skills_required:
• Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, XD)
• Figma for UI/UX design
• Colour theory, typography, layout principles
• Client communication and presentation
• Portfolio development and self-promotion
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Art, Design, and Mathematics helpful; minimum C
2. BSc / BA Graphic Design or Fine Art — 4 years
   (Kenyatta, Nairobi, USIU, KCA, Limkokwing Nairobi)
3. Diploma in Graphic Design (2–3 years)
4. Online certifications: Google UX Design, Adobe Certified Professional
5. Build a portfolio on Behance and Dribbble
fields.job_opportunities:
• Advertising agencies (Ogilvy Nairobi, Saatchi & Saatchi)
• Media and publishing houses
• Brand and marketing departments of corporations
• Tech startups needing UI/UX designers
• Freelance and agency work
• Digital marketing and social media agencies
fields.future_outlook: Digital transformation means every business needs visual design. UI/UX design is one of the highest-paying creative specialisations. Motion graphics and 3D design skills are increasingly demanded by media and entertainment companies. Remote freelance work gives Kenyan designers access to global client rates.

fields.title: Mechanical Engineer
fields.description: Mechanical engineers design, build, and maintain machines, engines, and mechanical systems — from industrial equipment and vehicles to HVAC systems and manufacturing lines.
fields.duties:
• Design mechanical components and systems using CAD software
• Analyse structural and thermal performance of machines
• Oversee manufacturing processes and quality control
• Maintain and troubleshoot industrial machinery
• Manage maintenance schedules and teams
• Ensure compliance with engineering and safety standards
fields.skills_required:
• Solid Works, AutoCAD, ANSYS for design and simulation
• Thermodynamics and fluid mechanics
• Manufacturing processes and materials science
• Project management
• Problem-solving and mechanical aptitude
fields.educational_pathway:
1. KCSE — Mathematics and Physics are essential
2. BSc Mechanical Engineering — 5 years (JKUAT, TU-K, UoN, Dedan Kimathi)
3. Graduate Engineer registration (Engineers Board of Kenya)
4. Specialisation: Automotive, Manufacturing, HVAC, Renewable Energy
5. Professional Engineer registration after 3 years practice
fields.job_opportunities:

fields.title: How KUCCPS Cluster Points Work: The Complete Guide for 2025
fields.author: CareerNext Editorial
fields.excerpt: Understanding how cluster points are calculated is the first step to choosing the right course. We break down the official KUCCPS formula in plain language.
fields.content:
Every year, thousands of KCSE candidates miss out on their preferred courses not because of poor grades, but because they do not understand how cluster points work. This guide explains everything.

WHAT ARE CLUSTER POINTS?

Cluster points are scores (out of 48) used by KUCCPS to rank students for specific courses. Each course belongs to a cluster group, and each cluster uses a specific combination of subjects to compute your score.

The official formula is:

Cluster Points = 48 x sqrt((core subjects total / 48) x (aggregate total / 84))

This means two things matter equally: how well you performed in the specific subjects a course cares about, AND your overall KCSE aggregate.

THE 7-SUBJECT AGGREGATE

Your aggregate (out of 84) is calculated using exactly 7 subjects:
- Mathematics (compulsory)
- Best of English or Kiswahili
- Your next 5 best subjects

The maximum aggregate is 84 points (12 points per subject x 7 subjects).

WHAT ARE CLUSTERS?

KUCCPS groups all degree, diploma and certificate programmes into 20 calculation clusters. For example:
- Cluster 1 (Pure Sciences): Maths, Biology, Chemistry, Physics
- Cluster 5 (Engineering): Maths, Physics, Chemistry
- Cluster 14 (Social Sciences): English/Kiswahili, History, Geography, CRE/IRE

Your score in the cluster that a course belongs to determines whether you qualify.

MINIMUM CLUSTER POINTS

Each course at every institution has a minimum cluster point cutoff. If your cluster points for that cluster exceed the cutoff, you qualify. If not, you do not -- regardless of your mean grade.

This is why a student with a B plain (mean grade) might qualify for Medicine while another with a B+ does not, if the B student had stronger scores in Biology, Chemistry and Physics specifically.

HOW TO IMPROVE YOUR CHANCES

1. Know which cluster your target course uses before your exam
2. Focus revision energy on the specific 4 subjects in that cluster
3. Use CareerNext to simulate different grade combinations and see how your cluster points change

Use the free calculator on this site to compute your exact cluster points for all 20 clusters instantly.

fields.title: Top University Courses With Accessible Cluster Point Cutoffs in Kenya
fields.author: CareerNext Research
fields.excerpt: Not all university courses require a B+ mean grade. These degree programmes have competitive cutoff points that C+ and B- students can realistically target.
fields.content:
Many students assume that university is out of reach unless they scored an A or B+. That is not true. KUCCPS lists dozens of degree programmes with cluster point cutoffs well within reach of C+ and B- students.

EDUCATION DEGREES

Bachelor of Education programmes -- particularly in Arts, Science and Special Needs -- regularly have cluster cutoffs in the 30-38 range. If you are passionate about teaching, this is a realistic and rewarding path.

AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES

Courses like BSc Agriculture, Horticulture and Food Science at many public universities have cutoffs in the 34-42 range. Kenya's growing agri-sector makes these graduates highly employable.

ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES

Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, and Forestry programmes attract fewer applicants than Medicine or Law, keeping cutoffs lower while career prospects remain strong.

SOCIAL WORK & COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

These programmes are vital for Kenya's development sector and NGO ecosystem. Cutoffs are typically in the 30-36 range.

LIBRARY & INFORMATION SCIENCE

An underrated but stable profession. Most universities offer this at cutoffs accessible to C+ students.

LINGUISTICS & LANGUAGE STUDIES

If you performed well in English or Kiswahili, Linguistics and Literature programmes could be your route into university.

RECORDS MANAGEMENT

A growing field as organisations digitise. Cutoffs remain competitive for students with a C+ aggregate.

PHYSICAL EDUCATION & SPORTS SCIENCE

If you are athletic and academically solid, this programme combines both and has accessible cluster point requirements.

HOW TO FIND YOUR SPECIFIC CUTOFFS

Use the CareerNext course finder to search by cluster points. Enter your grades, calculate your cluster points, and filter courses to see exactly which ones you qualify for.

fields.title: KMTC 2025 Intake: Everything You Need to Know
fields.author: CareerNext Editorial
fields.excerpt: Kenya Medical Training College opens two intakes per year. Here is a full breakdown of the application process, minimum grades, and most competitive programmes.
fields.content:
Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) is one of the most sought-after institutions in Kenya. With campuses in every county and over 50 health training programmes, it is the primary route into clinical and community health careers for diploma-level students.

INTAKES

KMTC typically runs two intakes per year:
- January/February Intake -- applications open around October/November
- September Intake -- applications open around June/July

MINIMUM ENTRY REQUIREMENTS

For most KMTC programmes, the minimum entry requirement is a mean grade of C (plain) in KCSE, plus specific subject requirements depending on the programme.

Most competitive programmes (such as Clinical Medicine and Pharmacy) require C+ and above, with strong grades in Biology, Chemistry and English.

TOP PROGRAMMES AND TYPICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Clinical Medicine & Surgery -- C+ overall, C+ in Biology, Chemistry and English
- Pharmacy -- C+ overall, B in Chemistry, C+ in Biology and Maths
- Nursing -- C overall, C+ in Biology and English
- Medical Laboratory Sciences -- C+ overall, C+ in Biology and Chemistry
- Health Records & Information Management -- C overall, C in English and Maths
- Community Health -- C overall, C in Biology
- Nutrition & Dietetics -- C overall, C+ in Biology and Chemistry

APPLICATION PROCESS

1. Visit the KUCCPS student portal (students.kuccps.net)
2. Log in with your KCSE index number and year
3. Select KMTC under institution type
4. Choose up to three programmes in order of preference
5. Submit and wait for placement results

TIPS FOR BETTER PLACEMENT

- List your most competitive programme first -- KUCCPS places you in the highest-ranked course you qualify for
- Check cluster point cutoffs from previous intakes to gauge your chances
- Consider county campuses -- they often have slightly lower competition than Nairobi campuses

Use CareerNext to calculate your cluster points for health-related clusters and see which KMTC programmes you qualify for.

fields.title: TVET vs University: Which Path Is Right for You?
fields.author: CareerNext Career Team
fields.excerpt: The choice between a university degree and a TVET diploma is not about which is better -- it is about which fits your goals, timeline and strengths.
fields.content:
One of the most important decisions after KCSE is choosing between university, TVET, KMTC or a TTC. Each path leads to a different destination. Neither is inferior -- they serve different goals.

UNIVERSITY DEGREES

Duration: 4-6 years
Entry: Minimum C+ for most programmes; A-B for competitive courses
Outcome: Bachelor's degree, eligible for professional registration in fields like Medicine, Law, Engineering

Best for students who:
- Scored C+ and above
- Want to enter professions that require degree-level qualification
- Are comfortable with a longer academic journey before employment
- Have a specific career in mind that is degree-gated (doctor, engineer, architect, lawyer)

TVET DIPLOMAS & CERTIFICATES

Duration: 1-3 years
Entry: D+ to C, depending on the programme
Outcome: Certificate or Diploma in a specific trade or technical skill

Best for students who:
- Scored below C+ in KCSE
- Want to enter the job market faster
- Are practically minded -- prefer building, making, fixing, or designing over classroom learning
- Want to start a business in a trade (welding, electrical, plumbing, fashion, ICT)

THE SALARY MYTH

Many families assume university graduates always earn more. This is increasingly not true. A qualified electrician or plumber running their own business often out-earns an Arts graduate on a starting salary. A TVET graduate with 3 years of experience can be more employable than a fresh degree holder in many sectors.

PROGRESSION ROUTES

TVET is not a dead end. Most colleges allow graduates to top up to a degree through bridging programmes. Diploma holders can join degree programmes at Part 2 in many universities, cutting the degree to 2-3 additional years.

THE HONEST QUESTION

Ask yourself: what problem do I want to spend my career solving? That answer -- not your KCSE grade -- should guide your choice.

Use CareerNext to explore both university and TVET courses side by side based on your actual cluster points.

fields.title: Understanding the KUCCPS Placement Process Step by Step
fields.author: CareerNext Editorial
fields.excerpt: From KCSE results to your first day on campus -- here is exactly how the KUCCPS placement system works and how to navigate it successfully.
fields.content:
The Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) is the body responsible for placing KCSE graduates into universities, KMTCs, TVETs, and TTCs. Understanding how it works gives you a significant advantage.

STEP 1: KCSE RESULTS

Once KNEC releases KCSE results (usually in December/January), your index number and results are automatically shared with KUCCPS. You do not need to do anything at this stage.

STEP 2: OPEN THE STUDENT PORTAL

Go to students.kuccps.net and log in using:
- Your KCSE Index Number (e.g. 12345678001)
- Your KCSE Year of Examination
- Your date of birth

STEP 3: MAKE YOUR COURSE CHOICES

You are allowed to select up to:
- 3 degree programmes (public universities)
- 3 KMTC programmes
- 3 TVET/TTC programmes

List your choices in order of preference. KUCCPS will place you in the highest-ranked course you qualify for.

STEP 4: PAY THE APPLICATION FEE

A small application fee (currently Ksh 1,500) is charged via M-Pesa. You cannot submit without payment.

STEP 5: PLACEMENT RESULTS

KUCCPS publishes placement results in batches. If you are placed, you will see your institution and course in the portal. If not placed in your first choices, you may be placed in revision rounds.

STEP 6: REVISION WINDOW

KUCCPS opens a revision window after the first placement round. This is your chance to change choices if you were not placed or if you want to try for a different course. Use this window wisely -- research cutoff points carefully before revising.

STEP 7: REPORTING TO CAMPUS

Once placed, you receive a joining letter with your campus reporting date. Bring your original KCSE certificate, ID, and placement letter.

COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID

- Choosing a course because of pressure from family without checking if you qualify
- Listing only highly competitive courses without any fallback choices
- Missing the revision window deadline
- Not verifying that your KCSE results in the portal are correct

Use CareerNext to simulate your placement -- calculate your cluster points, see which courses you qualify for, and plan your choices before the portal opens.

fields.title: Scholarships for Kenyan Students in 2025: Where to Apply
fields.author: CareerNext Research
fields.excerpt: From HELB loans to fully-funded international scholarships, here is a practical guide to funding your education after KCSE.
fields.content:
Financing higher education is one of the biggest challenges Kenyan students face. Fortunately, there are more options than most families realise.

HELB -- HIGHER EDUCATION LOANS BOARD

The most widely used funding source for Kenyan university students. HELB provides loans and bursaries to students at public universities.
- Loan amounts: Ksh 35,000-60,000 per year depending on financial need
- Repayment: Begins after graduation and employment
- Application: helb.co.ke after KUCCPS placement

HELB also offers bursaries (non-repayable) for students from very low-income households. Apply as early as possible -- bursary funds are limited.

GOVERNMENT SCHOLARSHIPS

The Kenya government occasionally offers full scholarships through specific programmes:
- Presidential Scholarship (high achievers, usually A grades)
- County Government Bursaries -- check with your county government office each year

EQUITY WINGS TO FLY

One of Kenya's most impactful scholarship programmes. Targets bright students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Graduates continue to benefit from alumni networks and mentorship.

MASTERCARD FOUNDATION SCHOLARS PROGRAM

Available at several Kenyan universities including University of Nairobi and Strathmore. Covers full tuition, accommodation, and a stipend. Targets academically strong students from low-income families. Applications usually open between January and March.

DAAD (GERMAN ACADEMIC EXCHANGE)

Germany offers generous scholarships for African students at German universities, taught in English. Strong in engineering, agriculture, and development studies.

KCDF -- KENYA COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION

Offers bursaries to students in TVET and university. Focus on marginalised communities. Apply via kcdf.or.ke.

PRACTICAL ADVICE

- Apply for multiple scholarships simultaneously -- there is no rule against it
- Start gathering documents early: KCSE certificate, birth certificate, ID, fee structure
- Write honest, specific personal statements -- generic applications rarely succeed
- Check your county and constituency bursary fund every year -- many local bursaries go unclaimed

Keep an eye on the CareerNext calendar page for updated scholarship deadlines.

fields.title: Career Spotlight: Clinical Medicine -- Kenya's Hidden Healthcare Pathway
fields.author: CareerNext Career Team
fields.excerpt: Clinical Officers are the backbone of Kenya's rural health system. Here is what the career looks like, what you study, and how to qualify.
fields.content:
When most students think about healthcare careers, they think of Medicine (MBChB) -- a 6-year degree requiring an A-minus or better. But Kenya's healthcare system runs largely on Clinical Officers, trained at KMTC in a rigorous 3-year diploma programme.

WHAT IS A CLINICAL OFFICER?

A Clinical Officer (CO) is a mid-level healthcare provider licensed to diagnose illnesses, prescribe medication, perform minor procedures, and manage patients -- particularly in district hospitals, health centres and dispensaries.

In rural Kenya, the Clinical Officer is often the most senior medical professional available. COs staff over 70% of Kenya's public health facilities.

WHAT DO YOU STUDY?

The KMTC Clinical Medicine and Surgery programme covers:
Year 1: Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, Medical Microbiology, Health Systems
Year 2: Internal Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, Gynaecology, Mental Health, Pharmacology
Year 3: Clinical rotations across all departments, Emergency Medicine, Community Health

HOW TO QUALIFY

Minimum requirements at KMTC:
- KCSE mean grade of C+
- C+ in Biology, Chemistry and English
- C in Mathematics (some campuses require C+)

CAREER PROGRESSION

After qualifying as a Clinical Officer, you can:
- Work in government facilities (salary Ksh 35,000-90,000+)
- Join a mission hospital or private clinic
- Specialise in Surgery, Anaesthesia, Ophthalmology, Psychiatry, or Paediatrics
- Pursue a Bachelor of Science in Clinical Medicine (upgrade degree, 2 years) at UoN or KU
- Work with international health organisations (MSF, WHO, UNHCR)

If you scored C+ in KCSE with strong Biology and Chemistry, Clinical Medicine at KMTC is a path worth serious consideration.

Use CareerNext to check whether your grades meet the KMTC Clinical Medicine requirements.

fields.title: 5 Mistakes Students Make When Choosing KUCCPS Courses
fields.author: CareerNext Editorial
fields.excerpt: Every placement cycle, thousands of students make avoidable errors that cost them their preferred courses. Do not be one of them.
fields.content:
The KUCCPS placement window is open for a limited time. Mistakes made during this period can lock you out of your preferred course for a full year. Here are the five most common errors and how to avoid them.

MISTAKE 1: CHOOSING COURSES WITHOUT CHECKING CLUSTER POINTS

Many students pick courses based on what they want to study, without verifying whether their cluster points actually meet the cutoff. Wanting to do Law is great -- but Law at UoN requires around 42 cluster points in Cluster 16. If your Cluster 16 score is 34, you will not be placed, no matter how much you want it.

Fix: Calculate your cluster points on CareerNext before opening the portal. Filter courses by your actual scores.

MISTAKE 2: LISTING ONLY HIGHLY COMPETITIVE COURSES

Putting Medicine, Law and Computer Science as your three choices without any fallback is a gamble. If you fall short of the cutoff for all three, you are left unplaced.

Fix: Use at least one safe choice -- a course you comfortably qualify for -- as your third option.

MISTAKE 3: IGNORING THE INSTITUTION DIFFERENCE

The same course at different universities can have dramatically different cutoff points. BSc Computer Science at JKUAT may have a lower cutoff than at UoN or Strathmore. If your score qualifies you for JKUAT but not UoN, listing only UoN means you miss out.

Fix: Search by course and compare cutoffs across multiple institutions.

MISTAKE 4: MISSING THE REVISION WINDOW

KUCCPS opens a revision window after initial placement results. Many students miss this window because they did not know it existed or missed the deadline.

Fix: Save the KUCCPS calendar dates on your phone. The revision window is typically 1-2 weeks long.

MISTAKE 5: CHOOSING BASED ON FAMILY PRESSURE, NOT FIT

Choosing a course because your parents want you to, without genuine interest or aptitude, is one of the most common causes of university dropout and career dissatisfaction in Kenya.

Fix: Take the CareerNext career quiz. It maps your interests and strengths to career clusters. Use the results as a starting point for an honest conversation with your family.

The placement process rewards students who are prepared. Use the tools available -- including this platform -- to make informed choices.

fields.question: What is CareerNext?
fields.answer: CareerNext is a fully accessible online platform that helps Kenyan KCSE graduates calculate their cluster points, discover which university, KMTC, TVET, and TTC courses they qualify for, and explore career options — all using the official KUCCPS formula and placement criteria.

fields.question: Is CareerNext the same as KUCCPS?
fields.answer:
No. KUCCPS (Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service) is the official government body that places students into institutions. You apply at kuccps.ac.ke.

CareerNext (this website) is an independent tool to help you prepare for that application — by calculating your points and finding your eligible courses before the portal opens. We are not affiliated with the government.

fields.question: How does CareerNext's pricing work?
fields.answer: Core tools — including the cluster points calculator, eligible courses list, course shortlist, and PDF exports — are fully accessible to all students. Some premium features, such as extended AI career chat credits and select resources, require a small one-time top-up. There is no subscription and no hidden charges.

fields.question: Do I need to create an account?
fields.answer: The cluster points calculator and basic course browsing are available without an account. However, creating an account unlocks: saving your grades between sessions, bookmarking courses to a watchlist, building a shortlist, tracking your applications, and getting personalised career engine recommendations.

fields.question: Is my data safe on CareerNext?
fields.answer: Yes. Your grades and personal information are stored securely and are never shared with third parties. We do not sell your data. You can delete your account at any time from your Profile settings.

fields.question: How are cluster points calculated?
fields.answer:
The official KUCCPS formula is:

Cluster Points = 48 × √( (cluster_subjects / 48) × (aggregate / 84) )

Where cluster_subjects is the sum of your raw marks in the 4 subjects that form each specific cluster (max 48), and aggregate is your KCSE total (max 84). The maximum possible cluster points score is 48.

fields.question: What is the KCSE aggregate (total)?
fields.answer:
The aggregate is your best 7 subjects scored as follows:

Mathematics + best of (English or Kiswahili) + your next 5 best subjects. The maximum aggregate is 84 points (7 subjects × A = 12 each).

fields.question: What are the 20 KUCCPS clusters?
fields.answer: KUCCPS has 20 subject clusters (C1–C20), each grouping 4 subjects relevant to a field of study. For example, Cluster 1 (Medicine) includes Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics. Visit the Clusters page to view all 20 clusters and their subject compositions.

fields.question: My cluster points seem lower than expected — why?
fields.answer:
A few common reasons:

• Weak cluster subjects — the formula weights your performance in the specific 4 cluster subjects heavily. A weak subject in the cluster drags the score down even if your overall grades are good.
• Low aggregate — the aggregate (all 7 best subjects) also factors in.
• Grade entry error — double-check you entered the correct grade for each subject, especially distinguishing A (12) from A- (11), etc.

fields.question: Can I enter grades from a photo of my result slip?
fields.answer: Yes. The calculator has an OCR (Optical Character Recognition) feature powered by GPT-4o. Take a clear, well-lit photo of your KNEC result slip and upload it — the system will attempt to read your grades automatically. If the photo is unclear, enter grades manually for best accuracy.

fields.question: What pathways does CareerNext cover?
fields.answer:
CareerNext covers all four KUCCPS placement pathways:

• Degree — Public and private universities (cluster-points based)
• KMTC — Kenya Medical Training College programmes (grade-based)
• TVET — Technical and Vocational Education Training institutions
• TTC — Teacher Training Colleges

fields.question: How do I find courses I qualify for?
fields.answer:
1. Go to the Cluster Points Calculator and enter your grades.
2. Click 'View Eligible Courses' — you'll see every course whose cutoff point is at or below your calculated cluster score.
3. Or use the Career Guidance Engine for a more personalised, filtered recommendation.

fields.question: What does 'cutoff points' mean?
fields.answer: The cutoff point is the minimum cluster score a student needed to be placed into a given course in a recent intake. If your cluster points are equal to or above the cutoff, you generally qualify. Cutoffs change each year based on applicant demand — a course in high demand may have a higher cutoff than its stated minimum.

fields.question: Why do some courses show a minimum grade instead of cluster points?
fields.answer: KMTC, TVET, and TTC programmes use minimum mean grade requirements (e.g. C, C+, B-) rather than cluster points. Only university degree courses use the cluster points system. When you use the Career Guidance Engine, select the appropriate pathway and you'll see the right criteria for each.

fields.question: Can I save and compare courses?
fields.answer:
Yes. When logged in, you can:
• Bookmark any course to your Watchlist (the bookmark icon on each course)
• Shortlist up to your top choices for easy comparison
• View cutoff trend charts to see how a course's cutoff has changed over the years
• Access everything from your Dashboard

fields.question: When does the KUCCPS application portal open?
fields.answer: The portal typically opens between June and August each year, after KCSE results are released. For 2026, the portal is estimated to open around 3 July 2026 and close around 21 August 2026. Check the official KUCCPS website and the KUCCPS Calendar on this site for confirmed dates.

fields.question: How many course choices can I submit on KUCCPS?
fields.answer: KUCCPS currently allows students to submit up to 4 course choices per pathway (degree, KMTC, TVET, TTC), ranked in order of preference. You are placed into the highest-ranked course you qualify for based on your cluster points and available slots.

fields.question: What happens if I don't get my first choice?
fields.answer: KUCCPS works through your ranked choices in order. If you don't qualify for your first choice (because your cluster points are below the cutoff or slots are filled), the system tries your second choice, then third, and so on. If none of your choices are successful, you may participate in the revision or inter-institutional transfer window.

fields.question: Does CareerNext submit my application to KUCCPS?
fields.answer: No. CareerNext is only a preparation and guidance tool. Your actual placement application must be submitted directly on the official KUCCPS portal at kuccps.ac.ke during the application window. CareerNext helps you decide what to apply for — you still complete the application yourself on the official site.

fields.question: What is the HELB loan and how do I apply?
fields.answer: The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides subsidised loans and bursaries to Kenyan students in accredited institutions. Applications are done online at helb.co.ke. Apply as soon as you get your placement letter — bursary deadlines are typically strict.

fields.question: How do I reset my password?
fields.answer: On the Login page, click 'Forgot password?'. Enter your email address and we'll send you a reset link. Check your spam/junk folder if you don't see it within a few minutes.

fields.question: Can I sign in with Google?
fields.answer: Yes — the login page has a 'Continue with Google' option powered by Google OAuth. Your CareerNext account will be linked to your Google account for quick sign-in on any device.

fields.question: How do I update my county or KCSE year?
fields.answer: Go to My Profile (accessible from the top-right account menu). You can update your full name, county, KCSE year, and profile picture there.

fields.question: Why does the Career Engine show sample courses instead of my results?
fields.answer: The 'Recommended For You' section on your dashboard shows real results only after you've run the Career Engine at least once. Visit the Career Guidance Engine, enter your grades and preferences, and click Proceed. Your dashboard will then display your personalised matches.

fields.question: How do I report an error in course data or cutoff points?
fields.answer: If you spot incorrect course information, outdated cutoff points, or a missing institution, please email us at hello@careernext.co.ke with details. We update the database regularly and appreciate corrections from students and educators.
